correctness.rationale: Binary lunar convolution gives S=A+B, with zero in each nonunit factor. Increasing paths in the addition grid give |S|≥|A|+|B|−1; in the equality cases, each monotone path exhausts S in order, so swapping two steps forces a_(i+1)−a_i=b_(j+1)−b_j in every cell. The only possible sizes yielding five are (2,3), (2,4), (3,3); the latter two give a progression, which also factors as {0,t}+{0,t,3t}. For (2,3) write S=B∪(B+x); exactly one collision corresponds to x equaling exactly one of the three positive pairwise differences of B. This yields the two families, and each family visibly factors. In F1, y<x gives m=2x and y choices 1,…,x−1; y>x gives m=x+y with x≤floor((m−1)/2) and y=2x excluded. Both branches are injective internally and can duplicate only at the progression: the third sorted element from the lower branch is m/2, so the upper branch must have third 2x=m/2, not y=m/2 (which would give y=x). In F2 the first two positive entries recover the unordered {x,y}; their interchange changes the maximum unless x=y, which is excluded. For intersection with F2 the third positive entry must be the sum of the first two. In F1 this gives y=3x in the upper branch or, in the lower branch, matching the maximum forces x=2y. Thus there is exactly one intersection iff 4 divides m, in addition to the internal duplicate in F1. Inclusion–exclusion gives C_m and choosing the three interior digits gives P_m and the claimed proportion. Fresh enumeration of all eligible factor shapes for 4≤m≤30 reproduced the exact family union, intersection and counts, including the m=4 endpoint.
residual_risks: Only the argument, not any finite enumeration, covers m>30 in this review. The frozen verifier's wider reported run is distinct recorded evidence.
